name: Halftone
summary: Tone printed as dots of different size or spacing; at a distance the dots merge into grey or colour.
how: Set the screen at 10 to 30 lines per cm for a print grain, or enlarge the dots to 4 to 8mm for a Pop effect.
Turn each colour screen to its own angle: cyan 15°, magenta 75°, yellow 0°, black 45°.

origin.note: Benjamin Day patents a mechanical tint of dots for printers; photographic halftone screens follow in the 1880s.

adoptions.via: The Daily Graphic of New York prints a photograph as a halftone.
Roy Lichtenstein paints enlarged Ben-Day dots by hand in Look Mickey.
Andy Warhol has photographs made into halftone screens and pulls them over hand-cut flat colour.
Punk zines photocopy halftones until the dots break up.
Duotone icon sets print each glyph in two tones of one hue, as a two-screen duotone does in print.
